item.title: Kofukuji Temple — Guide
item.description: Kofukuji, in the Teramachi temple district of central Nagasaki, is the oldest Chinese Ōbaku Zen temple in Japan, founded in 1620 by the city’s Chinese community. It was here that the influential Chinese monk Ingen (Yinyuan) first taught after arriving in Japan in 1654, effectively making Kofukuji the birthplace of the Ōbaku school of Zen in Japan — a sect that would go on to shape Japanese Buddhism, art and even cuisine.

item.title: Sofukuji Temple — Guide
item.description: Sofukuji, in the hills of central Nagasaki, is one of Japan’s finest and most colourful Chinese temples, founded in 1629 by the city’s Chinese residents from Fujian province. Belonging to the Ōbaku school of Zen — introduced to Japan from China in the seventeenth century — it is built in an authentic southern-Chinese Ming-dynasty style quite unlike Japanese temples, and vividly evokes Nagasaki’s role as Japan’s great port of Chinese trade.
